$( y - 2{)}^{2} = x - 1\text{and}x - 2y + 4 = 0$

questions.q: Let $S$ be the region bounded by the curves $y = x^{3}$~and $y^{2} = x$. The curve $y = 2\left|x\right|$~divides $S$ into two regions of areas ${R}_{1}$~and ${R}_{2}$.~If $max\left|{R}_{1}, {R}_{2}\right| = {R}_{2}$, then $\dfrac{R2}{R1}$& is equal to ______
questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.solution:
Intersection point of& $y^{2} = x \text{ and } y = 2 \left|$x\right|$~in the first quadrant will be~\left(\dfrac{1}{4}, \dfrac{1}{2}\right)

Also, intersection point of~$y = x^{3} & y^{2} = x$~in first quadrant will be~ \left(1, 1\right)$

Area of the region~$S = {∫}_{0}^{1}( $\sqrt{x} -$x^{3} )dx$~$= ${\dfrac{2x^{\dfrac{3}{2}}}{3} - \dfrac{x4}{4}}_{1}^{0}$~$= $\dfrac{5}{12}

Area of region~${R}_{1} = {∫}_{0}^{14}\$left(\sqrt{x} -2x\right)dx$~$= {\dfrac{2x^{\dfrac{3}{2}}}{3} -$x^{2}}_{0}^{14} = \dfrac{1}{48}$

$∴ {R}_{2} = S - {R}_{1} = \dfrac{19}{48}$

So,~$\dfrac{R2}{R1} =19$

questions.q:
Let $A$ be the area of the region~\left\{( x, y ) : y \ge x^{2}, y \ge ( 1 - x{)}^{2}, y \le 2x ( 1 - x )\right\}$.~Then $540A$ is equal to

$
questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.solution:
Given,

$A$ be the area of the region

\left\{( x, y ) : y \ge x^{2}, y \ge ( 1 - x{)}^{2}, y \le 2x ( 1 - x )\right\}$

Now solving~$y = x^{2} \text{ and } y = 2x \left(1 - x\right)$~we get,~$x = 0, $\dfrac{2}{3}

And solving~$y = \left(1 - x\right)2 \text{ and } y = 2x \left(1 - x\right)$~we get,~

$⇒ 1 + x^{2} - 2x = 2x - 2x^{2}$

$⇒ 3x^{2} - 4x + 1 = 0$

$⇒ x = 1, $\dfrac{1}{3}

Now on plotting the diagram of the above region we get,

Now from the above diagram area of the shaded region will be,

$A = {∫}_{13}^{23}\left(2x - 2x^{2}\right)dx - \left\{{∫}_{13}^{12}\left(1 - x\right)2dx + {∫}_{12}^{23}x^{2}dx\right\}$

$⇒ A = {x^{2} - $\dfrac{2x^{3}}{3}}_{13}^{23} - \left\${{\dfrac{\left(x - 1\right)3}{3}}_{13}^{12} + {\dfrac{x3}{3}}_{12}^{23}\right\}

$⇒ A = $\dfrac{5}{108}

$∴ A = $\dfrac{5}{108}$⇒ 540A = $\dfrac{5}{108} \times$540 = 25$

$

questions.q: If the line $y = mx$ bisects the area enclosed by the lines $x = 0, y = 0, x = \dfrac{3}{2}$ and the curve $y = 1 + 4x - x^{2},$~then $12m$ is equal to& <u>& & & & & & </u>.
questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.solution:
Given, the equation of line,& $y = mx$

And the line~$x = 0, y = 0, x = \dfrac{3}{2}$

The intersection point~ \left(\dfrac{3}{2}, 0\right)$

Area of triangle is half the total area~

$\dfrac{1}{2}{∫}_{0}^{3 / 2}\left(1 + 4x - x^{2}\right)dx = {∫}_{0}^{3 / 2}mxdx$

$\dfrac{1}{2}{x + 2x^{2} - \dfrac{x3}{3}}_{0}^{3 / 2} = \dfrac{m}{2}{x^{2}}_{0}^{3 / 2}$

\left(\dfrac{3}{2} + \dfrac{9}{2} - \dfrac{9}{8}\right) = \dfrac{9m}{4}$

$\dfrac{39}{8} = \dfrac{9m}{4}$

$m = \dfrac{39}{18}$

Then,~$12m$

$12m = \dfrac{39}{18} \times 12$

$12m = 26

questions.q:
Let for $x \in R$,~$f\left(x\right) = \dfrac{x + \left|x\right|}{2}$ and~$g\left(x\right) = \left\{
x,
x^{2},
x < 0
x \ge 0
\right$.~Then area bounded by the curve $y = \left(fog\right) \left($x\right)$ and the lines $y = 0, 2y - x = 15$& is equal to _____ .$
questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.solution:
We have,

$f\left(x\right) = \dfrac{x + \left|x\right|}{2} = \left\{
x; x \ge 0
0; x\right$

$g\left(x\right) = \left\{
x^{2}; x \ge 0
x; x\right$

So,

$fog\left(x\right) = f\left\{g\left(x\right)\right\} = \left[\begin{cases}g\left(x\right); & g\left(x\right) \ge 0 \\ 0; & g\left(x\right) < 0\end{cases}\right$

$⇒ fog\left(x\right) = \left\{
x^{2}; x \ge 0
0; x\right$

And,

$2y - x = 15$

Solving~$2y - x = 15$~and~$y = x^{2}$, we get

$2x^{2} - x - 15 = 0$

$⇒ x = \dfrac{1 \pm 11}{4}$

$⇒ x = 3, - \dfrac{5}{2}$

~

Required area

$A = {∫}_{0}^{3}\left(\dfrac{x + 15}{2} - x^{2}\right)dx + \dfrac{1}{2} \times \dfrac{15}{2} \times 15$

$⇒ A = {\dfrac{x2}{4} + \left(\dfrac{15}{2}\right)x - \dfrac{x3}{3}}_{0}^{3} + \dfrac{225}{4}$

$⇒ A = \dfrac{9}{4} + \dfrac{45}{2} - 9 + \dfrac{225}{4}$

$⇒ A = \dfrac{99 - 36 + 225}{4}$

$⇒ A = 72$

questions.q:
For real numbers& $a, b \left(a > b > 0\right)$, let

Area~ \left$\{ \left($x, y\right): x^{2} + y^{2} ≤ a^{2}\right$~and~\left\dfrac{x2}{a2} + \dfrac{y2}{b2} \ge$1\right\} = $30\pi

and

Area~ \left\{ \left($x, y\right): x^{2} + y^{2} ≥ b^{2}\right$~and~\left\dfrac{x2}{a2} + \dfrac{y2}{b2} \le$1\right\} = $18\pi

Then the value of \left($a - b\right)2$ is equal to _____.

$
questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.solution:
We know that area of circle& $= {πr}^{2}$~($r$~is radius of circle)~and area of ellipse~$= \pi ab$~(where $a \text{ and } b$~are length of semi major and semi minor axis)

Now given area between circle and ellipse $⇒ \pia^{2} - \piab = 30\pi$~ .....(i)

And~$⇒ \piab - \pib^{2} = 18\pi$~....(ii)

On subtracting equation (i) - (ii), we get~\left(a - b\right)2 = a^{2} - 2ab + b^{2} = 12$.

$

questions.q: Let a curve $y = y  \left(x\right)$~pass through the point  \left(3, 3\right)$~and the area of the region under this curve, above the $x$-axis and between the abscissae~$3$ and $x  \left(> 3\right)$~be~  \left(\dfrac{y}{x}\right)$3$. If this curve also passes through the point \left(\alpha,$6\sqrt{10}\right)~in the first quadrant, then $\alpha$is equal to _______.
questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.solution:
Given, the area of the region under this curve, above the $x$-axis and between the abscissae~$3$ and $x \left(> 3\right)$~be~ \left(\dfrac{y}{x}\right)$3$

So,~${∫}_{3}^{x}y d x = $\$left(\dfrac{y}{x}\right)3$

$⇒ x^{3}{∫}_{3}^{x}y d x = y^{3}$

Now differentiating both side w.r.t~$x$, we get

$⇒ x^{3}y + 3x^{2}\dfrac{y3}{x3} ==3y^{2}\dfrac{dy}{dx}~ \left\${\text{as given}{∫}_{3}^{x}$y d x = \left(\dfrac{y}{x}\right)$3\right\}$

$⇒ x^{4} + 3y^{2} = $3yx\dfrac{dy}{dx}

$⇒ $3xy\dfrac{dy}{dx} =$3y^{2} + x^{4}$

Now put~$y^{2} = t, $y\dfrac{dy}{dx} = \dfrac{1}{2}\dfrac{dt}{dx}

$⇒ $\dfrac{dt}{dx} - \dfrac{2}{x}$t = $\dfrac{2}{3}$x^{3}$

Now~$IF = e^{∫ - $\dfrac{2}{x}$dx} = $\dfrac{1}{x2}

So, solution is given by~

$t \timesIF = ∫ $\dfrac{2}{3}$x^{3} \timesIF$

$⇒ $\dfrac{t}{x2} = \dfrac{x2}{3} +$C$

Now given curve passes through ~ \left($3, 3\right)$~so~$C = - 2$

$⇒ \dfrac{y2}{x2} = \dfrac{x2}{3} -2$

So the equation of curve is~$3y^{2} = x^{4} - 6x^{2}$

Now curve also passes through~ \left(\alpha,$6\sqrt{10}\right)$

So,~${α}^{4} - 6{α}^{2} = 1080$

$⇒ $\alpha =$6$

$

questions.q: The area (in sq. units) of the part of circle $x^{2} + y^{2} = 169$ which is below the line $5x - y = 13$ is $\dfrac{\pi\alpha}{2\beta} - \dfrac{65}{2} + \dfrac{α}{β}\sin^{- 1} \left(\dfrac{12}{13}\right)$where \alpha, \betaare coprime numbers. Then \alpha + \betais equal to$
questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.solution:
Given: $x^{2} + y^{2} = 169, 5x - y = 13$

$⇒ x^{2} + \left(5x - 13\right)2 = 169$

$⇒ x^{2} + 25x^{2} + 169 - 130x - 169 = 0$

$⇒ 26x^{2} - 130x = 0$

$⇒ x\left(x - 5\right) = 0$

$⇒ x = 0, 5$

$⇒ y = - 13, 12$

So, the points of intersection are \left(0, - 13\right)\text{and} \left(5, 12\right)$.

So, the required area is given by,

$A = {∫}_{- $13}^{12}\sqrt{169 - y^{2}}$dy - $\dfrac{1}{2} \times$25 \times5$

$⇒ A = ${\dfrac{x}{2}\sqrt{169 - x^{2}} + \dfrac{169}{2}\sin^{- 1}\dfrac{x}{13}}_{- 13}^{12} - $\dfrac{1}{2} \times$25 \times5$

$⇒ A = $\dfrac{π}{2} \times \dfrac{169}{2} - \dfrac{65}{2} + \dfrac{169}{2}\sin^{- 1}\dfrac{12}{13}

Hence, on comparing with given value we get,

$⇒ $\alpha =$169, $\beta =$2$

$⇒ $\alpha + \beta =$171$

$

questions.q: The area of the region $S = \left\{( x, y ) : 3x^{2} \le 4y \le 6x + 24\right\}$ is______.
questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.solution:
We have,

$S = \left\{( x, y ) : 3x^{2} \le 4y \le 6x + 24\right\}$

Then,

$y = \dfrac{3x^{2}}{4}$

$4y = 6x + 24$

Solving both equations, we get~ \left(- 2, 3\right)$~and~ \left(4, 12\right)$.

Required area

$A = {∫}_{- 2}^{4}\left(\dfrac{6x + 24}{4} - \dfrac{3x^{2}}{4}\right)dx$

$⇒ A = \dfrac{1}{4}{∫}_{- 2}^{4}\left(6x + 24 - 3x^{2}\right)dx$

$⇒ A = {\dfrac{3}{4}x^{2} + 6x - \dfrac{x3}{4}}_{- 2}^{4}$

$⇒ A = \left(12 + 24 - 16 - 3 + 12 - 2\right)$

$⇒ A = 27sq . units

$

questions.q: If the area of the larger portion bounded between the curves $x^2+y^2=25$ and $y=|x-1|$ is $\frac{1}{4}(b \pi+c), b, c \in N$, then $b+c$ is equal to
questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.solution: $\begin{aligned} & \mathrm{x}^2+\mathrm{y}^2=5 \\ & \mathrm{x}^2+(\mathrm{x}-1)^2=25 \Rightarrow \mathrm{x}=4 \\ & \mathrm{x}^2+(-\mathrm{x}+1)^2=5 \Rightarrow \mathrm{x}=-3 \\ & \mathrm{~A}=25 \pi-\int_{-3}^4 \sqrt{25-\mathrm{x}^2} \mathrm{dx}+\frac{1}{2} \times 4 \times 4+\frac{1}{2} \times 3 \times 3 \\ & \mathrm{~A}=25 \pi+\frac{25}{2}-\left[\frac{\mathrm{x}}{2} \sqrt{25-\mathrm{x}^2}+\frac{25}{2} \sin ^{-1} \frac{\mathrm{x}}{5}\right]_{-3}^4 \\ & \mathrm{~A}=25 \pi+\frac{25}{2}-\left[6+\frac{25}{2} \sin ^{-1} \frac{4}{5}+6+\frac{25}{2} \sin ^{-1} \frac{3}{5}\right] \\ & \mathrm{A}=25 \pi+\frac{1}{2}-\frac{25}{2} \cdot \frac{\pi}{2} \\ & \mathrm{~A}=\frac{75 \pi}{4}+\frac{1}{2} \\ & \mathrm{~A}=\frac{1}{4}(75 \pi+2) \\ & \mathrm{b}=75, \mathrm{c}=2 \\ & \mathrm{~b}+\mathrm{c}=75+2=77\end{aligned}$

questions.q: Let the area of the region \left\{\left(x, y\right): \left|2x - 1\right| \le y \le \left|x^{2} - x\right|, 0 \le x \le 1\right\}$ be $A$. Then \left(6A + 11\right)2$& is equal to _____ .
questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.solution:
Given,

The area of the region \left\{\left(x, y\right): \left|2x - 1\right| \le y \le \left|x^{2} - x\right|, 0 \le x \le 1\right\}$ be $A$,

Now solving,

$x - x^{2} = 2x - 1$~

$⇒ x^{2} + x - 1 = 0$

$⇒ x = \dfrac{- 1 \pm \sqrt{5}}{2}$

And equating~$x - x^{2} = 1 - 2x$, we get~$x = \dfrac{3 \pm \sqrt{5}}{2}$

Now plotting the diagram of $y \ge \left|2x - 1\right|$~and~$y \le \left|x^{2} - x\right|$,

~

~

Now from diagram, both curve are symmetric about $x = \dfrac{1}{2}$

Hence, area of the bounded region is given by,

$A = \left|2{∫}_{3 - \sqrt{5}2}^{12}\left(\left(x - x^{2}\right) - \left(1 - 2x\right)\right)dx\right|$

$⇒ A = \left|2{∫}_{3 - \sqrt{5}2}^{12}\left(- x^{2} + 3x - 1\right)dx\right|$

$⇒ A = \left|2{\dfrac{- x^{3}}{3} + \dfrac{3}{2}x^{2} - x}_{3 - \sqrt{5}2}^{12}\right|$

$⇒ A = \dfrac{5\sqrt{5} - 11}{6}$

$⇒ 6A + 11 = 5\sqrt{5}$

$⇒ \left(6A + 11\right)2 = 125$.

$

questions.q: The graphs of sine and cosine functions, intersect each other at a number of points and between two consecutive points of intersection, the two graphs enclose the same area $A$. Then $A^{4}$ is equal to
questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.solution:
$A = {∫}_{\pi / 4}^{5\pi / 4} \left($sinx - cosx\right)dx$

$= \left(-$cosx - sinx\right)\left|{}_{\pi / 4}^{5\pi / 4}\right$

$= \left(- \left(\dfrac{- 1}{2}\right) - \left(\dfrac{- 1}{2}\right)\right) - \left(- \left(\dfrac{1}{2}\right) - \left(\dfrac{1}{2}\right)\right)$

$⇒ A = \dfrac{2}{2} + \dfrac{2}{2} ==2\sqrt{2}~sq. units

$⇒ A^{4} = \left(2\sqrt{2}\right)4 = 16 \times4 = 64$

$

questions.q: If the area of the region \left\{\left(x, y\right): \left|x^{2} - 2\right| \le y \le x\right\}$ is $A$, then $6A + 16\sqrt{2} is equal to ______________
questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.solution:
Given,

\left|x^{2} - 2\right| \le y \text{ and } y \le x$

Now on finding the intersection point we get,~ \left(x, y\right) ≡ \left(1, 1\right) & \left($2, 2\right)$

Now plotting the curve of the above function we get,

Now from above diagram required~bounded area will be,

$A = \left[{∫}_{1}^{2} \left($x - \left(2 - x^{2}\right)\right)dx + {∫}_{2}^{2}\left(x - \left(x^{2} - 2\right)\right)dx\right]$

$⇒ A = {\dfrac{x2}{2} - 2x + \dfrac{x3}{3}}_{1}^{2} + {\dfrac{x2}{2} - \dfrac{x3}{3} + 2x}_{2}^{2}$

$⇒ A = \left[1 - 2\sqrt{2} + \dfrac{2\sqrt{2}}{3}\right] - \left[\dfrac{1}{2} - 2 + \dfrac{1}{3}\right] + \left[2 - \dfrac{8}{3} +4\right] - \left[$1 - $\dfrac{2\sqrt{2}}{3} +2\sqrt{2}\right]

$⇒ A = $\dfrac{9}{2} - \dfrac{8\sqrt{2}}{3}

$⇒ 6A = 27 - $16\sqrt{2}

$⇒ 6A + $16\sqrt{2} =$27$

$

questions.q: Three points $O\left(0, 0\right), P\left(a, a^{2}\right), Q\left(- b, b^{2}\right), a > 0, b > 0,$ are on the parabola $y = x^{2}$. Let ${S}_{1}$ be the area of the region bounded by the line $PQ$ and the parabola, and ${S}_{2}$ be the area of the triangle $OPQ$. If the minimum value of $\dfrac{S1}{S2}$ is $\dfrac{m}{n}, gcd\left(m, n\right) = 1,$ then $m + n$ is equal to:
questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.solution:
Plotting the diagram of the given data we get,

Area of $△ OPQ$ is given by,

${S}_{2} = \dfrac{1}{2}\left|\begin{cases}0 & 0 & 1 \\ a & a^{2} & 1 \\ - b & b^{2} & 1\end{cases}\right|$

$⇒ {S}_{2} = \dfrac{1}{2} \left(ab^{2} + a^{2}b\right) . . . \left($i\right)$

Now, equation of line $PQ: y - a^{2} = $\dfrac{a^{2} - b^{2}}{a + b} \left($x - a\right)$

$⇒ y - a^{2} = \left(a - b\right)x - \left(a - b\right)a$

$⇒ y = \left(a - b\right)x + ab . . . \left(ii\right)$

Area bounded by the line $PQ$ and the parabola is given by,

${S}_{1} = \mathop{∫}_{- b}^{a} \left( \left($a - b\right)x + ab - x^{2}\right)dx$

$⇒ {S}_{1} = {\left($a - b\right)\dfrac{x2}{2} + \left(ab\right)x - \dfrac{x3}{3}}_{- b}^{a}$

$⇒ {S}_{1} = \dfrac{\left(a - b\right)2 \left($a + b\right)}${2} +$ab \left($a + b\right) - \left($a^{3} + b^{3}\right)3 . . . \left($iii\right)$

$⇒ $\dfrac{S1}{S2} = \dfrac{\dfrac{\left(a - b\right)2}{2} + ab - \left(a^{2} + b^{2} - ab\right)3}{ab2}

$⇒ $\dfrac{S1}{S2} = \dfrac{3\left(a - b\right)2 + 6ab - 2\left(a^{2} + b^{2} - ab\right)}{3ab}

$⇒ $\dfrac{S1}{S2} = \dfrac{3\left(a^{2} + b^{2} - 2ab\right) + 6ab - 2\left(a^{2} + b^{2} - ab\right)}{3ab}

$⇒ $\dfrac{S1}{S2} = \dfrac{3a^{2} + 3b^{2} - 6ab + 6ab - 2a^{2} - 2b^{2} + 2ab}{3ab}

$⇒ $\dfrac{S1}{S2} = \dfrac{a^{2} + b^{2} + 2ab}{3ab}

$⇒ $\dfrac{S1}{S2} = \dfrac{1}{3} \left[\dfrac{a}{b} + \dfrac{b}{a} +$2\right]$

$⇒ \left(\dfrac{S1}{S2}\right)$min = $\dfrac{1}{3} \left[1 + 1 + 2\right]\left\{\text{as}\dfrac{a}{b} + \dfrac{b}{a} \ge2\right\}$

$⇒ \left(\dfrac{S1}{S2}\right)min = \dfrac{4}{3}$

$⇒ m + n = 7$

$

questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.solution:
Given:

$2y^{2} = 3x, x + y = 3\left(slopeis - 1\right) \text{ and } \left(x - 3\right)2 + y^{2} = 2$

Now plotting the diagram of the above function we have,

So, required area is

$A = {∫}_{0}^{32}\left(3 - y - \dfrac{2y^{2}}{3}\right)dy - \dfrac{\pi\left(\sqrt{2}\right)2 \times {45}^{°}}{360 °}$

$⇒ A = {3y - \dfrac{y2}{2}}_{0}^{32} - \dfrac{2}{3}{\dfrac{y3}{3}}_{0}^{32} - \dfrac{π}{4}$

$⇒ A = \dfrac{21}{8} - \dfrac{π}{4}$

So,

$A = \dfrac{1}{4} \left(\dfrac{21}{2} - \pi\right)

$⇒ $\pi +$4A = $\dfrac{21}{2}

$⇒ 4\left(\pi +$4A\right) = 42$

questions.q: If the area enclosed by the parabolas ${P}_{1}: 2y = 5x^{2}$~and ${P}_{2}: x^{2} - y + 6 = 0$~is equal to the area enclosed by ${P}_{1}$~and $y = \alphax, \alpha > 0$, then ${α}^{3}$& is equal to _____ .
questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.solution:
Given:

${P}_{1}: 2y = 5x^{2}$

${P}_{2}: x^{2} - y + 6 = 0$

On solving both equations, we have

$2y = 5 \left(y - 6\right)$

$⇒ 3y = 30$

$⇒ y = 10$

$⇒ x = \pm2$

So, points of intersection are~ \left(2, 10\right) & \left(-$2, 10\right)$.

Also, solving~${P}_{1}$~and~$y = \alphax$, we have

$x = 0, $\dfrac{2\alpha}{5}

According to question~$2{∫}_{0}^{2} \left(x^{2} + 6 - \dfrac{5x^{2}}{2}\right)dx = {∫}_{0}^{2\$alpha5} \left(\alphax - \dfrac{5x^{2}}{2}\right)dx$

$⇒ 2{\dfrac{x3}{3} +$6x - $\dfrac{5x^{3}}{6}}_{0}^{2} = {\dfrac{\alphax^{2}}{2} - \dfrac{5x^{3}}{6}}_{0}^{2\alpha5}$

$⇒ $2\left($12 + \dfrac{8}{3} - \dfrac{20}{3}\right) = \left[\dfrac{2{α}^{3}}{25} - \dfrac{8{α}^{3}}{6 \times 25}\right]$

$⇒ \dfrac{2{α}^{3}}{75} =16$

$⇒ {α}^{3} = 600$

$

questions.q: If& $A$~is the area in the first quadrant enclosed by the curve~$C: 2x^{2} - y + 1 = 0$, the tangent to~$C$~at the point~  \left(1, 3\right)$~and the line~$x + y = 1$, then the value of~$60A$& is................$
questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.solution:
Given,

$y = 2x^{2} + 1$

Now tangent to above equation at~ \left(1, 3\right)$~is given by,

$y - 3 = 4 \left(x - 1\right)$

$⇒ y = 4x - 1$

Now plotting the diagram we get,

Required area of bounded region will be,

$A = {∫}_{0}^{1}\left(2x^{2} + 1\right)dx - \text{area of}△ QOT - \text{area of}△ PQR + \text{area of}△ QRS$

$⇒ A = \left(\dfrac{2}{3} +1\right) - \dfrac{1}{2} - \dfrac{9}{8} + \dfrac{9}{40} = \dfrac{16}{40}$

$⇒ 60A = 16$

$
